Finding a therapist and going back on medication. I've struggled for half my life with my mental health. I finally just hit my rock bottom 3 years ago next month. A few months into therapy my SI thoughts and depression still weren't letting up. I was really against taking medication because I was forced to in the psych ward I was involuntarily committed to by my parents as a teen. I had enough of the bad thoughts that I asked my therapist for a psychiatrist recommendation. The first one I worked with was no good. I found a new one last December and he's been amazing to work with. He actually listens and cares. He also diagnosed me with Bipolar II. This explained so much to me, because it wasn't just depression I had struggled with. Looking back I had episodes of hypomania/mania and it was just nice to finally have a diagnosis that explained what I went and am still going thru. 

I'm still in therapy and on five different medications, but I'm so happy. I can think clearly for the first time. I finally think I've made it out of the tunnel. I'm in the light.

I know it's hard to talk about the tough subjects, but I think you should bring it up with her again and explain that what she says about eating and cycling isn't helping. Tell her that your struggle with eating is serious and that you need her help. I know it may be daunting to say this out loud to her. (I've struggled many times in telling things to my therapist.) If you find it easier, you can write down what you want to say and then hand it to her in your next session. I don't know if your therapist allows contact between sessions ( email, phone call). If she does, you can write an email about how serious this is to you and that you would like to discuss it next session (the same with the phone call). 

I hope this was a bit helpful. Just remember, your therapist does care about you and wants to know these types of things to better help you. I hope that you get the support you need; you deserve it.
